sites.name: Hyundai Motor Manufacturing Alabama (HMMA) - Montgomery AL
sites.dossierExcerpt:
Roster coords (32.280312, -86.324154, ROOFTOP) landed directly on the HMMA
main assembly building — confirmed by satellite: a giant white building
carrying the "HYUNDAI" wordmark and logo on its roof. Web research
(hmmausa.com, Wikipedia) confirms HMMA is a 1,744-acre campus, 3.4M sq ft of
buildings, producing Santa Fe / Tucson / Elantra / Santa Cruz. No relocation
needed; center nudged slightly to the assembly hall.

fieldNotes.site: 1,744-acre HMMA campus (per hmmausa.com / Wikipedia). Operational developed footprint geofenced here is ~620 acres; full owned land much larger. 3.4M sq ft of buildings: stamping, weld, paint, assembly, three engine shops, plus an east logistics/parts warehouse complex and a 2-mile test track at the north edge.
fieldNotes.truckGate: HMMA uses controlled, numbered gates (web research confirms 'Gate 2' as the visitor entrance). Main multi-lane entry off Hyundai Blvd at 32.2769,-86.3253; access control is set back inside the property, standard for a large guarded automotive campus.
fieldNotes.guardShack: Inferred true — large captive-OEM assembly plant with numbered, staffed security gates is industry-standard. A security/check-in structure is visible inside the entry road near the dock-side at ~32.2799,-86.3252. Booth not crisply resolvable at road edge, hence medium-confidence on exact footprint.
fieldNotes.dropArea: Large dedicated trailer drop yard on the SE/east side off Hyundai Blvd (~32.2788,-86.3145) holding ~80-100 trailers, plus extensive trailer rows along the logistics warehouse faces. dropArea 50+.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: East logistics/parts warehouse complex shows long banks of dock doors with trailers backed in on multiple faces; assembly building has additional truck docks. Total across the site comfortably 50+; 90 is an honest overhead estimate.
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: Campus with 12+ distinct large buildings (assembly hall, stamping, paint, three engine shops, multiple logistics warehouses) — clear multi-facility campus.
fieldNotes.shipRcvSeparate: Inbound parts logistics warehouses (east complex) are physically separate from the assembly-building shipping docks — distinct dock clusters on different parts of the campus.
fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: Main entry is a wide multi-lane apron with abundant paved width — physical room for an express/bypass lane.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Surrounded by farmland and woods on the south edge of Montgomery; rural-edge setting.
fieldNotes.scale: No truck scale positively identified in imagery; flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.railServed: No rail spur observed running into the developed campus footprint.
fieldNotes.trailersVisible: Honest overhead estimate (~220) across drop yard and warehouse dock faces; counts approximate.
fieldNotes.geofence: Center 32.2812,-86.3235. Perimeter box covers the developed operational footprint (buildings, lots, test track) — the YardFlow-relevant geofence — not the full 1,744-acre land parcel.

fieldNotes.scale: No truck scale identified; flagged uncertain.

sites.name: Glovis America Vehicle Processing Center - West Point GA
sites.dossierExcerpt:
The roster coordinate (32.911036, -85.137392 / 2000 Webb Rd) lands at the
southwest tip of the Kia Georgia (KaGA) automotive campus. A z20 satellite probe
at that exact point shows only an open paved parking-lot apron off Webb Rd — not
a building. Web research (glovisusa.com locations; CMac.ws / YellowPages
directory listings; Automotive Logistics feature) confirms Glovis America
operates a Vehicle Processing Center co-located on the KaGA campus where Kia
opened its assembly plant in late 2009. Glovis is Hyundai Motor Group's captive
finished-vehicle 3PL. The auditable "facility" is the VPC vehicle-marshaling and
processing operation on the campus — not the empty roster pixel — so the center
was locked on the core vehicle-storage lots at 32.9130, -85.1315.

fieldNotes.siteSelection: Roster point (2000 Webb Rd) lands at an open paved parking-lot entrance off Webb Rd at the SW tip of the Kia Georgia (KaGA) / Glovis campus. The Glovis Vehicle Processing Center is the finished-vehicle marshaling/processing operation co-located on the KaGA campus; audited the VPC vehicle-storage yards and rail facility rather than the empty roster pixel. Locked center on the core vehicle lots at 32.9130,-85.1315.
fieldNotes.facilityType: Finished-vehicle Processing Center: no traditional loading docks. Vehicles move by car-carrier truck and rail. dockDoorCount=0 and dockDoors=NONE reflect VPC layout, not a missing count.
fieldNotes.railServed: Confirmed - multiple parallel auto-rack rail spurs run directly into the vehicle yards on the NW side (probe rail.png), classic VPC rail receiving/shipping.
fieldNotes.dropArea: 50+ - tens of thousands of finished-vehicle stalls in marked rows fill the southern and western lots; this is the dominant feature of the site. Counted as vehicle storage, not box-trailer drop, but dropArea band reflects massive vehicle marshaling capacity.
fieldNotes.truckGate: Medium confidence. The KaGA/Glovis campus is a secured private facility with controlled access; no Street View inside. Internal guard/checkpoint structure visible near campus interior roads (gate2.png). Public-road Street View at Webb Rd shows only an open employee-lot apron. Car-carrier trucks enter through a controlled campus gate - treated as truckGate true / remoteGs not certain.
fieldNotes.guardShack: Could not positively confirm a staffed booth at the car-carrier gate from imagery; small internal structures present. Left guardShack false, remoteGs true as best estimate; flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: True - the property is a large campus with the Kia assembly plant building cluster plus separate Glovis VPC processing buildings and rail yard.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Rural - West Point GA, small town; campus surrounded by forest and farmland with an I-85 interchange nearby.
fieldNotes.siteAreaAcres: ~385 acres for the audited VPC vehicle-yard perimeter; the full KaGA campus including the assembly plant is far larger (~2000+ acres).

sites.name: Glovis America Port Vehicle Processing - Brunswick GA
sites.dossierExcerpt:
A z15 satellite probe at the roster point lands inside the Georgia Ports
Authority (GPA) Colonel's Island Terminal at the Port of Brunswick. Web research
(GPA facilities page, glovisusa.com locations, Automotive Logistics) confirms
Colonel's Island is a ~1,700-acre roll-on/roll-off auto terminal with multiple
on-terminal vehicle processors; Glovis America operates as one of those
processors and Brunswick is the nation's busiest RoRo port. The on-terminal
processors share the secured terminal's gate, fence line and storage, so the
audit treats the GPA secured terminal as the facility. Center placed on the
terminal core at 31.1270, -81.5390.

fieldNotes.siteSelection: Roster point (1 Joe Frank Harris Blvd) lands inside the Georgia Ports Authority Colonel's Island Terminal at the Port of Brunswick - confirmed via web research (GPA facilities page, glovisusa.com, Automotive Logistics). Colonel's Island is a ~1,700-acre RoRo auto terminal with multiple on-terminal vehicle processors; Glovis America operates as one of those processors. The audited facility is the GPA secured terminal as a whole, since the on-terminal processors share the gate, fence line and storage. Center placed on the terminal core at 31.1270,-81.5390.
fieldNotes.facilityType: Port / RoRo vehicle import-export processing terminal. No traditional loading docks - vehicles roll on/off ships at the RoRo berths and move within the terminal by drive-away and by rail. dockDoorCount=0 / dockDoors=NONE reflect this.
fieldNotes.railServed: Confirmed - a curved auto-rack rail loop runs into the terminal on the west side (probe rail.png), used for rail receiving/shipping of finished vehicles.
fieldNotes.truckGate: TRUE. The terminal is a fully secured GPA port facility (TWIC-controlled). All vehicular traffic funnels across a single 4-lane divided causeway and through a controlled main gate complex before reaching the storage and processing areas.
fieldNotes.guardShack: TRUE (medium confidence). A secured GPA port terminal of this class operates a staffed main gate complex; small gate-area structures are visible. Exact booth identification flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.backupSensitive: TRUE - the entire terminal is served by ONE causeway access road; any queue at the gate would back up along the single causeway with no alternate route. High chokepoint sensitivity.
fieldNotes.multiStep: TRUE (best estimate, flagged uncertain) - secured port terminals typically run a multi-stage check (port gate, then processor/yard checkpoints). Marked truck-staging grids are visible inside the terminal.
